items.followUp: State two rules for writing the scientific name of an organism.

rubric.why: A binomial name has two parts.
rubric.description: Names the two parts of a binomial name.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the generic and specific names.

rubric.why: The capitalization rule distinguishes the two parts.
rubric.description: Gives the capitalization rule for the two parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the genus begins with a capital letter and the species name with a lowercase letter.

modelAnswer: A scientific name consists of two words: the genus name and the species name.
The genus name begins with a capital letter, while the species name begins with a lowercase letter.

items.followUp: What is facilitated diffusion, and how does it differ from active transport?

rubric.why: Movement against the concentration gradient distinguishes active transport from passive transport.
rubric.description: States the direction of movement in active transport.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that substances move against their concentration gradient.

rubric.why: Active transport requires energy to move substances against the gradient.
rubric.description: States that active transport requires energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning energy or ATP.

modelAnswer: Active transport is the movement of substances across a cell membrane against their concentration gradient.
It requires energy, usually supplied by ATP.

items.followUp: State one difference between the cell membrane and the cell wall.

rubric.why: The primary wall forms while the cell is still growing.
rubric.description: Describes when the primary cell wall forms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the primary wall forms first, during cell growth.

rubric.why: The secondary wall is deposited after cell growth and is generally thicker.
rubric.description: Describes the secondary cell wall in contrast.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the secondary wall forms after growth, or that it is thicker than the primary wall.

modelAnswer: The primary cell wall forms first, while the cell is growing, and is usually thin and flexible.
The secondary cell wall is deposited inside the primary wall after cell growth and is usually thicker.

items.followUp: Name the two main stages of the cell cycle and briefly describe each.

rubric.why: Interphase is one of the two main stages of the cell cycle.
The mitotic phase is the other main stage of the cell cycle.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the mitotic phase or M phase.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the sequence of events a cell undergoes from one cell division to the next.
Its two main phases are interphase and the mitotic phase (M phase).

items.followUp: What happens during interphase and during mitosis?

rubric.why: Karyokinesis refers to division of the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the nucleus divides.

rubric.why: Cytokinesis refers to division of the cytoplasm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cytoplasm divides.

modelAnswer: Karyokinesis is the division of the nucleus.
Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm, separating the cell into daughter cells.

items.followUp: How do carbon dioxide concentration and water availability affect the rate of photosynthesis?

rubric.why: Increasing light intensity raises the rate until another factor limits it.
rubric.description: States the effect of light intensity on photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate increases with light intensity, at least until it reaches a limiting or saturation point.

rubric.why: Photosynthesis is enzyme-controlled, so temperature increases the rate only up to an optimum.
rubric.description: States the effect of temperature on photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate rises to an optimum temperature and falls above it.

modelAnswer: As light intensity increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases until it reaches a saturation point.
As temperature rises, the rate increases up to an optimum; above the optimum, the rate falls because photosynthetic enzymes are affected.

items.followUp: Name the main nutrients required in a balanced human diet.

rubric.why: Carbohydrates, proteins and fats are major nutrients in food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming any two of carbohydrates, proteins and fats.

rubric.why: Vitamins, minerals, water and roughage are also components of a balanced diet.
rubric.description: Names any two other food components.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming any two of vitamins, minerals, water and roughage (dietary fibre).

modelAnswer: The components of human food include carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, water and roughage (dietary fibre).

items.followUp: What is meant by vitamins? State two functions of vitamin C.

rubric.why: Vitamins are organic substances required in small quantities for normal body functions and growth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing vitamins as organic substances needed in small quantities for normal growth or body functions.

rubric.why: Vitamin A supports vision and maintains healthy epithelial tissues, including the skin.
rubric.description: Gives two functions of vitamin A.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both a role in vision and a role in maintaining healthy skin or epithelial tissues.

modelAnswer: Vitamins are organic compounds required in small quantities for normal growth and body functions.
Vitamin A is needed for normal vision and helps maintain healthy skin and epithelial tissues.
